# 佛說四無所畏經

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

T775 in one fascicle is a brief sūtra-translation by [施護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%BD%E8%AD%B7) (Dānapāla, fl. 980–1017) at the Northern Sòng Translation Bureau in Kāifēng. The title 四無所畏 (*sì wúsuǒwèi*) translates Skt. *catur-vaiśāradya* — the four "fearlessnesses" or "self-confidences" of a *Tathāgata* — one of the standard *abhidharma* enumerations of the Buddha's exclusive epistemic and ethical perfections.

**Abstract**

The four *vaiśāradya* of a buddha, as enumerated in the standard *abhidharma* tradition (cf. *[Abhidharma-kośa](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0023)* book 7) and in the *prajñāpāramitā* and *bodhisattva-piṭaka* literature, are: (1) confidence in proclaiming *full and perfect awakening* — i.e. that he has attained complete *bodhi* and that no opponent can rightly contradict the claim; (2) confidence in proclaiming *the destruction of all defilements* — that all *āsravas* are extinguished in him; (3) confidence in *teaching the path* — that the path he expounds leads to the cessation of suffering for those who practise it; (4) confidence in *teaching the obstacles* — that the *dharmas* he identifies as obstacles to the path are indeed obstacles. The Buddha's four *vaiśāradya* are paired in scholastic literature with the *daśa-bala* (ten powers — see [KR6i0479](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0479) and [KR6i0480](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0480)) as the basic enumeration of the exclusive properties of buddhahood.

Dānapāla's brief Chinese rendering is a free-standing exposition of the *catur-vaiśāradya* doctrine in *sūtra*-frame, suitable for recitation and study. The *vaiśāradya* doctrine is given fuller treatment in the *[Mahā-prajñā-pāramitā-śāstra (T1509)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0019)* of [Nāgārjuna](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BE%8D%E6%A8%B9) and in the *[Daśabhūmika-vyākhyāna](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0006)* of [Vasubandhu](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%96%E8%A6%AA); the Sòng Bureau's stand-alone sūtra-translation provides Chinese audiences with the doctrine in its short narrative form.
